questions.question: In Thomas Carlyle's 'Sartor Resartus' (1833–1834), what is the name of the German Professor of 'Things-in-General' who progresses from the 'Everlasting No' to the 'Everlasting Yea'?
questions.explanation: Professor Diogenes Teufelsdröckh of Weissnichtwo authors the treatise on Clothes and undergoes spiritual rebirth on the Rue Saint-Thomas de l'Enfer.

questions.question: In which London periodical was Thomas Carlyle's 'Sartor Resartus' first serialized between November 1833 and August 1834?
questions.explanation: Sartor Resartus was serialized in Fraser Magazine in 1833-1834 before Ralph Waldo Emerson arranged its first book edition in Boston in 1836.

questions.question: In Book II of 'Past and Present' (1843), whose twelfth-century Latin chronicle did Thomas Carlyle use to recount the heroic rule of Abbot Samson?
questions.explanation: Published by the Camden Society in 1840 the Chronicle of Jocelin of Brakelond inspired Carlyle portrait of twelfth-century Abbot Samson.

questions.question: What central argument in John Henry Newman's 'Tract 90' (1841) outraged Protestant authorities and brought 'Tracts for the Times' to an end?
options: That the King of England had no legal authority to collect ecclesiastical tithes
That the Book of Common Prayer should be replaced by the Latin Vulgate
That Anglican bishops must renounce their seats in the House of Lords
That the Thirty-Nine Articles were compatible with Roman Catholic doctrine
questions.explanation: Newman argued in Tract 90 that the Thirty-Nine Articles condemned only popular Papal abuses rather than official Council of Trent decrees.

questions.question: Which Anglican novelist and Christian Socialist provoked John Henry Newman into writing 'Apologia Pro Vita Sua' (1864) by questioning his devotion to truth?
questions.explanation: In the January 1864 issue of Macmillan Magazine Charles Kingsley casually charged that Newman and the Roman clergy did not value truth for its own sake.

questions.question: Which monthly magazine, edited at the time by William Makepeace Thackeray, halted the serialization of John Ruskin's 'Unto This Last' in 1860 after reader protests?
questions.explanation: Publisher George Smith and editor Thackeray stopped Ruskin socialist essays in The Cornhill Magazine after four installments between August and November 1860.

questions.question: Which painting by James Abbott McNeill Whistler did John Ruskin attack in 'Fors Clavigera' (1877) as 'flinging a pot of paint in the public's face', sparking a famous libel suit?
options: Symphony in White, No. 1: The White Girl
Harmony in Blue and Gold: The Peacock Room
Nocturne in Black and Gold: The Falling Rocket
questions.explanation: Exhibited at the Grosvenor Gallery in 1877 Whistler Nocturne in Black and Gold led to the 1878 trial where Whistler won a single farthing in damages.

questions.question: To which fellow Cambridge Apostle did Alfred Tennyson dedicate 'The Palace of Art' (1832), warning him that a purely aesthetic life divorced from love cannot stand?
questions.explanation: Trench had remarked to Tennyson at Trinity College Cambridge that they could not live in art alone prompting the introductory poem to The Palace of Art.

questions.question: Whose joyful October 1842 marriage at Boxley does Alfred Tennyson celebrate in the Epilogue ('O true and tried, so well and long') to 'In Memoriam A.H.H.' (1850)?
options: His sister Emily Tennyson and Captain Richard Jesse
His sister Cecilia Tennyson and his friend Edmund Lushington
His own 1850 marriage to Emily Sellwood at Shiplake
His brother Charles Tennyson and Louisa Sellwood
questions.explanation: The Epilogue celebrates the wedding of Cecilia Tennyson and Glasgow Greek professor Edmund Lushington anticipating the birth of a higher human race.

questions.question: What is the subtitle of Alfred Tennyson's 1847 blank-verse narrative poem 'The Princess', in which Princess Ida founds an academy solely for women?
questions.explanation: Tennyson subtitled The Princess A Medley and added the famous intercalary lyrics such as Tears Idle Tears in the third edition of 1850.

questions.question: In Robert Browning's 1855 dramatic monologue 'Fra Lippo Lippi', which powerful Florentine ruler protects the Carmelite painter when he is caught out at night?
questions.explanation: Lippi tells the captain of the watch that he lodges in the palace of Cosimo of the Medici who commissioned his painting.

questions.question: From which character's mad song in Act III, Scene 4 of Shakespeare's 'King Lear' did Robert Browning take the title of 'Childe Roland to the Dark Tower Came' (1855)?
options: The Earl of Kent in the stocks
questions.explanation: In King Lear Edgar disguised as Poor Tom chants Child Rowland to the dark tower came His word was still Fie foh and fum.

questions.question: In Robert Browning's 'The Ring and the Book' (1868–1869), who is the seventeen-year-old Roman child-wife fatally stabbed by her husband Count Guido Franceschini?
questions.explanation: Dying over four days from twenty-two dagger wounds Pompilia delivers her luminous deathbed monologue in Book VII of The Ring and the Book.

questions.question: In 'The Ring and the Book', which young canon of Arezzo helps the pregnant Pompilia flee from Count Guido's palace toward Rome?
questions.explanation: Canon Giuseppe Caponsacchi delivers the passionate monologue of Book VI defending his chivalric rescue of Pompilia.

questions.question: In Elizabeth Barrett Browning's verse novel 'Aurora Leigh' (1856), who is the Christian-socialist cousin whose condescending proposal Aurora rejects before uniting with him at the end?
questions.explanation: Romney Leigh turns Leigh Hall into a Fourierist phalanstery is blinded when the hall burns down and finally weds Aurora as an equal partner.

questions.question: Under what pseudonym did Robert Buchanan initially publish his October 1871 article 'The Fleshly School of Poetry: Mr. D. G. Rossetti' in 'The Contemporary Review'?
questions.explanation: Buchanan signed his Contemporary Review attack with the pseudonym Thomas Maitland before expanding it into a signed pamphlet in 1872.

questions.question: Under what title did Dante Gabriel Rossetti publish his December 1871 defense in 'The Athenaeum' replying to Robert Buchanan's attack?
questions.explanation: Rossetti published The Stealthy School of Criticism in The Athenaeum on 16 December 1871 condemning Buchanan pseudonymous attack.

questions.question: From whose coffin at Highgate Cemetery was the manuscript notebook of Dante Gabriel Rossetti's 'Poems' (1870) exhumed in October 1869?
questions.explanation: Stricken with remorse after Elizabeth Siddal laudanum overdose in 1862 Rossetti buried his poems in her hair and had Charles Augustus Howell exhume them in 1869.

questions.question: What name did Gerard Manley Hopkins give to his prosodic meter that scans verse by stressed syllables with variable numbers of unstressed syllables?
questions.explanation: Hopkins developed sprung rhythm in The Wreck of the Deutschland 1875-1876 allowing one stress to be followed by zero to three slack syllables.

questions.question: To whom did Gerard Manley Hopkins add the explicit dedication beneath the title of his 1877 sonnet 'The Windhover'?
questions.explanation: Written at St Beuno in May 1877 Hopkins called The Windhover the best thing he ever wrote and added the dedication To Christ our Lord in 1884.

questions.question: How many narrative tales—two for each month of the year, alternating between Classical and Medieval sources—comprise William Morris's 'The Earthly Paradise' (1868–1870)?
questions.explanation: Framed by Norse wanderers meeting Greek descendants on a western island Morris The Earthly Paradise tells twenty-four tales across the twelve months.

questions.question: In Algernon Charles Swinburne's 'Poems and Ballads' (1866), which poem spoken by a fourth-century Roman pagan contains the line 'Thou hast conquered, O pale Galilean'?
questions.explanation: Subtitled After the Proclamation in Rome of the Christian Faith Hymn to Proserpine quotes the dying words attributed to Emperor Julian the Apostate.

questions.question: Which Scottish professor coined the term 'Spasmodic School' and parodied Philip James Bailey, Sydney Dobell, and Alexander Smith in his 1854 hoax 'Firmilian'?
questions.explanation: Writing as T Percy Jones in Blackwood Magazine in May 1854 William Edmonstoune Aytoun demolished the Spasmodic vogue with Firmilian.

questions.question: How does Charles Dickens uniquely structure the narrative voice across the sixty-seven chapters of 'Bleak House' (1852–1853)?
options: Between a third-person present-tense narrator and Esther first-person past narrative
Through four conflicting courtroom depositions presented directly to the Lord Chancellor
By assigning each of the nineteen monthly numbers to a different Chancery law clerk
Through weekly confidential letters exchanged between Mr. Jarndyce and Inspector Bucket
questions.explanation: Thirty-four chapters are told by an impersonal present-tense narrator and thirty-three chapters are narrated in the past tense by Esther Summerson.

questions.question: Which illiterate rag-and-bottle shop dealer—nicknamed the 'Lord Chancellor' in Dickens's 'Bleak House'—dies by spontaneous combustion while hiding a valid Jarndyce will?
questions.explanation: In Chapter 32 Krook perishes by spontaneous combustion leaving behind a greasy soot and the hidden later will of Jarndyce.

questions.question: In Charles Dickens's 'Little Dorrit' (1855–1857), what is the name of the obstructive government department run by the Barnacle family whose motto is 'How not to do it'?
questions.explanation: Introduced in Book I Chapter 10 the Circumlocution Office satirizes British governmental incompetence exposed during the Crimean War.

questions.question: In Charles Dickens's final completed novel 'Our Mutual Friend' (1864–1865), who is the wealthy heir who assumes the alias John Rokesmith after being reported drowned in the Thames?
questions.explanation: Returning from the Cape to claim his father dust-heap fortune on condition he marry Bella Wilfer John Harmon poses as the secretary John Rokesmith.

questions.question: At the end of Chapter 32 of Thackeray's 'Vanity Fair' (1847–1848), during which historic 1815 battle is Amelia Sedley's husband Captain George Osborne killed?
questions.explanation: In one of the most famous single sentences in English fiction Thackeray reveals that George Osborne is lying dead at Waterloo with a bullet through his heart.

questions.question: Who is the reserved English Protestant narrator of Charlotte Brontë's 1853 novel 'Villette', who teaches at Madame Beck's pensionnat and loves Professor Paul Emanuel?
questions.explanation: Drawing on Charlotte Brontë own experiences at the Pensionnat Heger in Brussels Lucy Snowe narrates Villette 1853.

questions.question: In Emily Brontë's 'Wuthering Heights' (1847), what date is carved above the farmhouse door beside 'Hareton Earnshaw', and what year opens Mr. Lockwood's diary?
options: 1588 above the door and 1798 in Lockwood's diary
1649 above the door and 1815 in Lockwood's diary
1500 above the door and 1801 in Lockwood's diary
1600 above the door and 1847 in Lockwood's diary
questions.explanation: Wuthering Heights opens with the exact date 1801 and in Chapter 1 Lockwood pauses to admire the date 1500 and name Hareton Earnshaw over the front door.

questions.question: What was the title of Mary Ann Evans's witty October 1856 essay in 'The Westminster Review' that mocked the 'mind-and-millinery', 'oracular', and 'white neck-cloth' species of popular fiction?
options: The Natural History of German Life
questions.explanation: Published just before she began Scenes of Clerical Life Silly Novels by Lady Novelists defined George Eliot commitment to psychological realism.

questions.question: In George Eliot's 'Middlemarch' (1871–1872), what is the title of the futile comparative treatise on world religion upon which Reverend Edward Casaubon wastes his life?
options: A Harmony of the Ancient Fathers
questions.explanation: Unaware of modern German scholarship Casaubon compiles endless notebooks for his unfinishable Key to All Mythologies.

questions.question: Who is the ambitious young reformist physician in 'Middlemarch' who seeks to discover the 'primitive tissue' of human anatomy before being ruined by debt and marriage to Rosamond Vincy?
questions.explanation: Dr Tertius Lydgate comes to Middlemarch with high scientific ideals but is compromised by his alliance with the banker Bulstrode and his materialistic wife Rosamond.

questions.question: Which 1876 novel—George Eliot's final novel—contrasts the destructive marriage of Gwendolen Harleth to Henleigh Grandcourt with the title hero's Zionist mission?
questions.explanation: In Daniel Deronda 1876 Deronda rescues Mirah Lapidoth meets the visionary Mordecai and departs for the East to help establish a Jewish national homeland.

questions.question: Who is the rose-cultivating Scotland Yard detective summoned to investigate the theft of the yellow Indian diamond in Wilkie Collins's 'The Moonstone' (1868)?
questions.explanation: Modeled on real Scotland Yard Inspector Jonathan Whicher of the Road Hill House case Sergeant Cuff deduced that the smear on the painted door came from Rachel nightgown.

questions.question: In Wilkie Collins's 'The Moonstone' (1868), who is proved by Ezra Jennings's medical reenactment to have taken the diamond while sleepwalking under the influence of laudanum?
questions.explanation: Unknowingly dosed with laudanum by Dr Candy Franklin Blake took the diamond in his sleep to protect it and handed it to Godfrey Ablewhite.

questions.question: In Mary Elizabeth Braddon's sensation novel 'Lady Audley's Secret' (1862), what was the true first-married name of the bigamist 'Lucy Graham' before she married Sir Michael Audley?
questions.explanation: Born Helen Maldon she married dragoon officer George Talboys faked her death in the newspaper became the governess Lucy Graham and pushed George down a well.

questions.question: Which vast, dark tract of Wessex heathland dominates the entire opening chapter ('A Face on which Time Makes but Little Impression') of Thomas Hardy's 'The Return of the Native' (1878)?
questions.explanation: Egdon Heath serves as a brooding tragic protagonist in The Return of the Native mirroring the fates of Eustacia Vye and Clym Yeobright.

questions.question: By what grim nickname is Jude Fawley's morbid young son known in Thomas Hardy's 'Jude the Obscure' (1895), who hangs his half-siblings and himself leaving the note 'Done because we are too menny'?
questions.explanation: Sent from Australia by Arabella Donn the boy called Little Father Time kills Sue two children and himself in their Christminster lodging.

questions.question: In George Gissing's 'New Grub Street' (1891), which conscientious, uncompromising novelist is destroyed by poverty and overwork, in contrast to the opportunistic journalist Jasper Milvain?
questions.explanation: Unable to churn out commercial three-decker potboilers Edwin Reardon loses his wife Amy and dies in poverty after Jasper Milvain marries her.

questions.question: The 'yellow-backed French novel' lent by Lord Henry Wotton that poisons Dorian Gray's mind is widely identified with which 1884 decadent novel by Joris-Karl Huysmans?
questions.explanation: Under cross-examination at his 1895 trial Oscar Wilde confirmed that the poisonous book in Chapter 10 of Dorian Gray was Huysmans 1884 novel À rebours.

questions.question: In Act I of Oscar Wilde's 'The Importance of Being Earnest' (1895), in the cloak-room of which London railway station—specifically on 'the Brighton line'—was the infant Jack Worthing found in a handbag?
questions.explanation: Jack tells the horrified Lady Bracknell that Mr Thomas Cardew found him in a large black leather handbag in the cloak-room at Victoria Station The Brighton line.

questions.question: In 'The Importance of Being Earnest', what is the name of Cecily Cardew's governess who twenty-eight years earlier absent-mindedly placed her three-volume novel in a perambulator and the baby in a handbag?
questions.explanation: Laetitia Prism identifies the handbag with a stain from the exploding temperance beverage revealing that Jack is truly Algernon elder brother Ernest.

questions.question: Which 1885 philosophical novel by Walter Pater, set in second-century Rome under Marcus Aurelius, traces a young Roman's spiritual journey from Epicureanism toward early Christianity?
questions.explanation: Pater wrote Marius the Epicurean His Sensations and Ideas in 1885 to clarify the ethical meaning of the Conclusion to The Renaissance.

questions.question: Which seminal 1884 critical essay did Henry James publish in 'Longman's Magazine' in reply to Walter Besant, defining the novel as 'a personal, a direct impression of life'?
questions.explanation: Published in September 1884 Henry James The Art of Fiction rejected didactic rules and prompted Robert Louis Stevenson reply A Humble Remonstrance.

questions.question: In which 1877 critical lecture and essay did George Meredith argue that true Comedy requires social equality between men and women and awakens 'thoughtful laughter'?
options: On the Idea of Comedy and of the Uses of the Comic Spirit
questions.explanation: Delivered at the London Institution in February 1877 Meredith An Essay on Comedy celebrated Molière Congreve and the silvery laughter of the Comic Spirit.

questions.question: Which 1899 critical book by Arthur Symons, dedicated to W. B. Yeats, introduced French Symbolist poets such as Mallarmé, Verlaine, and Rimbaud to English readers?
questions.explanation: Arthur Symons 1899 study The Symbolist Movement in Literature profoundly shaped W B Yeats T S Eliot and Ezra Pound.

questions.question: At which historic Fleet Street tavern in London did W. B. Yeats, Ernest Dowson, and Lionel Johnson regularly gather after founding the Rhymers' Club in 1890?
questions.explanation: Founded in 1890 by Yeats and Ernest Rhys the Rhymers Club met upstairs at Ye Olde Cheshire Cheese in Fleet Street and published two anthologies in 1892 and 1894.

questions.question: Which of the following statements concerning Victorian literature (1832–1901) is NOT correct?
options: Charles Dickens left 'The Mystery of Edwin Drood' unfinished at his death in 1870
The Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood was founded in London in 1848
Charles Darwin published 'On the Origin of Species' in November 1859
Gerard Manley Hopkins served as Poet Laureate immediately after Tennyson's death in 1892
questions.explanation: Hopkins died in June 1889 with his major poems unpublished; Alfred Austin was appointed Poet Laureate in 1896 after Tennyson death.

questions.question: Which of the following character-and-work pairings from the Victorian Period (1832–1901) is NOT correctly matched?
options: Bathsheba Everdene — Thomas Hardy's 'Far from the Madding Crowd'
Becky Sharp — William Makepeace Thackeray's 'Vanity Fair'
questions.explanation: Michael Henchard is the tragic protagonist of Thomas Hardy 1886 novel The Mayor of Casterbridge whereas Obadiah Slope and Mrs Proudie appear in Barchester Towers.
